theme: How fast resistance spreads once you start dosing
title: Resistance Sweep Forecast — the fitness cost hides in the flat line
strategies: constant 0.5 (ignores the data entirely) -> reproduces the checker baseline ~0.1

greedy: average the visible pre-treatment readings and extrapolate that value FLAT -- an honest, noise-reduced read of the data, but blind to the mechanism; correct until the dosing plan starts, then wrong by up to the full sweep amplitude

strong: the pre-treatment level is a mutation/transfer-selection EQUILIBRIUM, not an arbitrary constant -- invert it (c = (mu+tau)/p0) to recover the hidden fitness cost, then plug that cost into the SAME replicator dynamics with the given dosing rate to get the closed-form post-treatment trajectory

headroom above strong: better denoising of the equilibrium estimate (e.g. down-weighting outlier readings, or a maximum-likelihood fit instead of the plain mean) tightens the recovered cost and pushes held-out error toward the measurement-noise floor
